## Did the robot pick up the cup? {#cup-evidence}

## What did the robot know? {#physical-ai-loop}

**Observe** · A camera sees the cup.

**Choose** · A learned policy asks the hand to close.

**Act and observe again** · The hand moves. Where is the cup now?


## What would you save from a failed grasp? {#armnet-data}

Three camera views, joint measurements and the commands sent.

::: {.fragment}
ArmnetBench recorded **37 successes in 255 block-stacking attempts** on low-cost arms.
:::

::: {.footnote}
[ArmnetBench · Table 2 · Nov 2, 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.03168v1) · [Released recordings](https://huggingface.co/datasets/armnet/armnetbench_v01_lerobot_so101)
:::

## What does a reduction gear change? {#gear-trade}

An ideal 3:1 gear at steady speed

| | Motor shaft | Joint shaft |
|:---|:---:|:---:|
| Turns per second | 3 | 1 |
| Torque | 1 N·m | 3 N·m |

::: {.footnote}
[Lynch & Park, *Modern Robotics*, §8.9](https://modernrobotics.northwestern.edu/nu-gm-book-resource/8-9-actuation-gearing-and-friction/)
:::


## Could the arm do this for an hour? {#repeat-lift}

The arm lifted one full cup.

What would you record if it lifted a cup every ten seconds?

::: {.fragment}
Watch the motor temperature and count completed lifts.
:::


## How far does the elbow have to go? {#joint-error}

The target angle is 30°.

| Sensor reading | Angle still to go |
|:---:|:---:|
| 20° | 10° |
| 28° | 2° |


## Which correction should be larger? {#proportional-correction}

The elbow has 10° left to go. Later it has 2° left.

::: {.fragment}
With the same gain, a larger gap gives a larger correction.

$$u = K_p (r - y)$$
:::

## Who chooses the next target? {#two-loops}

A learned policy can ask the hand to move toward the cup.

A joint controller measures the elbow angle and corrects its motion.

## How did Atlas learn what its motors could do? {#nov-motor-model data-seconds="130"}

Measure the real motors.

Match the simulated motors to those measurements.

Train in simulation, then try the movement on wheels.

::: {.footnote}
[Boston Dynamics · Atlas on a Roll · Nov 9, 2026](https://bostondynamics.com/blog/atlas-on-a-roll/)
:::

## Why are these experiments possible now? {#why-now}

Affordable arms can record repeated attempts, including failures.

Policies can command how hard a robot should press.

Measured motors make simulated practice closer to real motion.


## Would you trust the next lift? {#transfer}

A new robot lifts one box beside a person.

What would you check before it lifts the next hundred?

::: {.fragment}
Count attempts, dropped boxes and human interventions.
:::
